workload.description: Dropbox-shaped sync/share: metadata-heavy listing, bulk bytes via object storage

components.name: File API — auth, metadata, presigning (m6i.large x6)

monthly_cost_per_instance.measured_context: m6i.large — AWS EC2 us-east-1 / On-Demand / Linux / shared tenancy / 730 h per month; instance-hour only (excludes EBS, data transfer); x86-64 (Intel Ice Lake). Band: zero-width: within the pinned scope the hourly list rate is a single exact published number with no variance. Month length (672-744 h), burstable credit surcharges, Savings Plans and Spot are OUT-OF-BAND modifiers, named per row, not band edges.

citations.note: $0.096/h x 730 = 7008c/month. Cross-checked to the cent against the AWS Price List Bulk API (version 20260904231117).

monthly_cost_per_instance.measured_context: cache.t4g.medium — AWS ElastiCache us-east-1 / On-Demand / Redis engine / standard support / 730 h per month; node-hour only. Band: zero-width at the Redis/Memcached standard-support rate. The Valkey engine is CHEAPER and Extended Support is DEARER; both are different products/support states, not a price range for this row, so they are named here rather than used as band edges.

components.name: PostgreSQL — file tree, versions, ACLs, share links

monthly_cost_per_instance.measured_context: db.m6i.large — AWS RDS PostgreSQL us-east-1 / On-Demand / Single-AZ (band high = Multi-AZ) / 730 h per month; INSTANCE-HOURS ONLY (excludes storage, provisioned IOPS and backup above the free allocation). Band: deployment spread: low = Single-AZ, high = Multi-AZ. Both are on-demand, standard-tier, us-east-1 PostgreSQL, so the band is fully in scope. Multi-AZ is ~2x Single-AZ.

citations.note: $0.178/h Single-AZ x 730 = 12994c/month. MySQL/MariaDB run ~3.9% cheaper than PostgreSQL for the same class.

components.name: Post-upload pipeline: virus scan, thumbnails, sync fan-out

monthly_cost_per_instance.measured_context: kafka.t3.small — AWS MSK us-east-1 / On-Demand / provisioned broker / 730 h per month; broker-hour only (excludes storage and data transfer). Band: zero-width: single published broker-hour rate in the pinned scope.

assumptions.subject: workload
assumptions.statement: 3,000 req/s peak across ~1M active users: 45% folder listings, 30% downloads, 15% uploads, 7% share-link operations, 3% sync polls

assumptions.subject: cache
assumptions.statement: 75% hit-rate on folder listings; sync polls hit the cache 90% of the time (the answer is usually 'nothing changed')

assumptions.subject: store
assumptions.statement: BYTES DO NOT FLOW THROUGH THE APP TIER. Clients get a presigned URL and talk to the object store directly, so the app tier is sized for metadata operations only. The engine still counts one store visit per download/upload, which is the request, not the byte stream

assumptions.subject: store
assumptions.statement: Egress 175,000 GB/month is derived, not observed: ~900 downloads/s at peak, an assumed 30% average-to-peak ratio (270/s) and a 256 KB average object. A media-heavy mix moves this by an order of magnitude

assumptions.subject: cost
assumptions.statement: At the default $0.09/GB internet rate, egress is the LARGEST line in this design — larger than all compute combined. That is the real economics of file hosting. Volume CDN or R2-style zero-egress contracts change it materially and are not modelled

assumptions.subject: q
assumptions.statement: Every upload publishes one event to a 3-broker Kafka cluster for virus scanning, thumbnailing and sync fan-out to the user's other devices. The ASYNC WORKERS behind the queue are not modelled as components — the v1 engine models request paths, not background consumers, so their capacity is not checked here

assumptions.subject: cost
assumptions.statement: Object-store REQUEST charges are not modelled (only storage and egress are). The engine carries a single request rate, and it is API-gateway shaped ($3.00 per million); S3 GET is roughly $0.40 per million and PUT roughly $5.00 per million, so a single rate cannot represent both honestly. At 1,350 store operations/s this is a real omission, on the order of a few hundred dollars a month against a $20k bill

_library.summary: Sync-and-share file service: metadata in Postgres, blobs in object storage via presigned URLs.
